Use Tier 2: deepen the existing GRURec with a causal prefix-mean embedding feature, focusing on model_design and training_evaluation. The successful GRU reaches macro validation HR@10=0.5737, while sampled softmax regressed and gated attention failed to execute. A plausible remaining limitation is that the recurrent state compresses persistent user interests; explicitly retaining an aggregate of previous item embeddings tests this hypothesis without introducing another attention mechanism.

In GRURec.encode, compute the cumulative sum of the existing shared item embeddings divided by cumulative nonpadding counts, so each position receives information only from its observed prefix. Normalize this prefix representation, concatenate it with the raw GRU state, and apply one learned linear projection initialized to select the GRU state and ignore the added feature. Feed the fused representation through the existing dropout, projection, normalization, and scoring head, retaining tied item embeddings, learned item bias, and the independent positive/negative softplus objective. Mask padding explicitly and clamp prefix counts for empty histories; the added feature is jointly trained within the same network and produces no separate scores.

Keep history sampling, eight uniform negatives, optimizer, learning rate, epoch limit, and early stopping unchanged to isolate this architectural change. Update checkpoint metadata and the predictor writer together, preserving identical chronological truncation, right padding, last-valid-state selection, and exactly one newly trained checkpoint per category. Verify causal prefix behavior, finite empty-history outputs, and checkpoint reload parity, then compare pinned-host macro validation HR@10 and all four category scores against 0.5737 using the existing fixed validation protocol. Preserve the supplied splits, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, single-GPU execution, and shared search budget; leave hidden-test evaluation to the host.
